subject: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection — follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acme.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection — follow-up from discovery call

Hi Sofia / Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the quick run-through of Acme's GDPR and procurement requirements. Recap and next steps below: 

1) Our ask from you: can you confirm whether Acme will require Redwood to sign the standard DPA (we can use our template) or whether you need us to complete your DPA request form? You mentioned a short internal review of which is preferred.

2) SCC module: you asked which SCC module we recommend. From our side (and based on the architecture you described), Redwood typically supports Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) when the customer is the controller and Redwood acts as processor. If you expect Acme to be the processor for any data flows, let us know and we will discuss Module Three.

3) SOC 2 / HIPAA: quick status — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in-scope (report available under NDA) and we support HIPAA-covered workloads via Business Associate Addendum (BAA). If you need either artefact, we can share the SOC 2 report and our BAA template next week after an NDA / DPA is agreed.

4) Vendor security questionnaire: please send over the questionnaire (or HubSpot link) and we'll start the intake. We can usually return the completed questionnaire within 3–5 business days.

Attached: ACME_DPA_Request_Form.pdf (placeholder) and an SCC_Comparison_Table.xlsx that outlines typical module choices and implications.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm preferred DPA path (Redwood DPA vs. your form) — Sofia/Liam
- Confirm controller/processor alignment — Acme legal
- I'll follow up with our DPA template and the SCC recommendation once we hear back (cc'ing Rishi to help with legal artefacts).

Would you like a 30-minute follow-up next Wednesday to align on the DPA/SCC selection? I'm available 10:00–12:00 CET.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — helpful. A couple quick clarifications from legal: 

- Acme will be the Controller for the majority of data flows described (customer PII, account data). That suggests Module Two is the right place to start.
- Please confirm in writing that Redwood will act as Processor and will not use Acme data for any other purpose than providing the service (we'll need that in the DPA).
- We have a short DPA request form (attached) — I've filled the first tab but left the legal questions for Redwood. Could you complete and return?

Also, can you share your SOC 2 cert or an access link (we can sign an NDA if required)? We prefer to review that in-parallel.

If Module Two is Redwood's recommendation, please include the justification and the specific SCC module reference in the DPA response. If you could get back to us by Friday, that would keep our procurement timeline on track.

Thanks,
Liam

Marissa / Neha — see suggested language below. I've updated Redwood_Processor_DPA_v3.docx with the exact wording and an SCC justification paragraph; attaching the edited doc and the SCC_Comparison_Table.xlsx. Also included SOC 2 access instructions.

Suggested processor confirmation (one sentence):
"Redwood Inference will act solely as a Processor of Personal Data on behalf of Acme Corp for the provision of the Redwood inference service and will not use, retain, or disclose Personal Data for any purpose other than as necessary to provide the services described in the Agreement, except as required by law."

SCC recommendation justification (short paragraph):
"Based on the described data flows (Acme retains control over Customer PII and decides processing purposes), Redwood recommends the EU SCC Module Two (Controller-to-Processor). Module Two maps to our standard technical and organizational measures: encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls, role-based segregation, KV cache isolation per tenant, and contractual commitments in our DPA and security annex. This module provides the appropriate contractual safeguards while aligning with Redwood's processor role."

SOC 2 access instructions: we can share the most recent SOC 2 Type II report via our secure portal. Please have Acme sign the attached standard NDA (link in doc) and provide an e-mail for portal access. Once NDA is in place, we will provide a time-limited download link and a point of contact for follow-up questions.
